papers.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models
papers.desc: We present EchoWM, an omnimodal world model for enterable generative media that responds to continuous navigation while jointly generating 720p video, environmental sound, music and speech.

papers.title: Towards a Densing Law for User Representation Learning at Billion-Scale Capacity
papers.desc: User representation learning in real-world industrial scenarios is commonly scaled by increasing user amount, behavioral sequence length and model size.

papers.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
papers.desc: Policy optimization (PO) for Large Language Models faces a stability--exploration trade-off, currently mediated by an action-side Policy-KL regularizer.

papers.title: One Success Isn't Reliability: Thinkingbox, a Sandbox and Benchmark for Agents in Stateful Business Workflows
papers.desc: Recent agent benchmarks increasingly ground evaluation in executable environments, from code repair to web navigation, app APIs, and function calling.

papers.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out
papers.desc: Autonomous research systems are increasingly capable of executing long research workflows, yet automation alone does not ensure that the resulting process remains scientifically grounded.

papers.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs
papers.desc: Serving large language models cheaply increasingly means shipping models that are both structurally compressed to a fraction of their parameters and quantized to 4 bits.

papers.title: One Polluted Page Is Enough: Evaluating Web Content Pollution in LLM Recommenders
papers.desc: Search-augmented LLMs increasingly mediate everyday consumer recommendations by retrieving live web content.

papers.title: LongWoF-Bench: Evaluating EvoMap Genes for Verifiable Long-Workflow Tasks
papers.desc: Large language models are increasingly expected to execute complex workflows whose success depends on maintaining interdependent constraints and producing artifacts that satisfy strict end-to-end verification.

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Privacy-Aware Federated Biosignal Learning
papers.desc: Electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings are sensitive biomedical data, limiting the ability of hospitals and wearable devices to share raw signals for centralized model training.

papers.title: RIBOSPAN: A Long-Context RNA Foundation Model for Versatile RNA Modeling
papers.desc: Full-length RNAs, particularly messenger RNAs, often exceed the context lengths used to pretrain existing RNA foundation models, limiting complete-transcript modeling at single-nucleotide resolution.

papers.title: Industrial-Instruction: An End-to-End Framework for Building Instruction-Tuning and Benchmark Datasets from Industrial Technical Reports
papers.desc: Industrial technical reports contain high-value knowledge for maintenance, troubleshooting, and product engineering, but their heterogeneous structure (dense prose, specifications, tables) makes them difficult to index and reason over with standard retrieval and QA pipelines, and no public instruction-tuning or benchmark datasets are built from such documents.

papers.title: EXPL-FR: Explaining Face Recognition Models via Vision-Language Alignment
papers.desc: Deep face recognition (FR) models reach near-saturated accuracy but remain opaque: a practitioner cannot ask which semantic attributes a similarity score relied upon.

papers.title: Tomatoes, Potatoes, and Onions: Questioning the Need for Faces in Face Presentation Attack Detection
papers.desc: Face presentation attack detection (PAD) is traditionally formulated as a face-specific problem, although many of the visual artifacts introduced by print, replay, and recapture processes are not inherently tied to facial appearance.

papers.title: WorldToken: Time-First Sequence Modeling for Robotic Imitation Learning
papers.desc: Robot policies receive heterogeneous observations at each decision step, yet sequence models differ in how they organize these inputs over time.

papers.title: From Generation to Simulation: How Far Are World Models from Being True Simulators?
papers.desc: With the rapid progress of diffusion models and large-scale video generation, generative world models are increasingly expected to replace traditional simulators, including physics engines, game engines, and reinforcement-learning environments.
